payload.question_text: Strands and LangGraph aren't used anywhere in the repo. What should the /tmp rewrite do?
The 3 Strands unit tests pass. A real test sends live Bedrock calls, and the agents write files (handoffs, configs, logs) under workloads/. Where should that run?
Which AWS profile/region and Bedrock model should the real run use?

The real Bedrock run left changes in workloads/customer_orders/: 8 tracked files rewritten (semantic.yaml + 7 test files) plus new handoffs, a MANUAL_DAG file, extra tests, specs, rendered scripts, run/*, and reviews/ and logs/ at the repo root. Revert them?

origin is the public GitHub repo aws-samples/sample-Agentic-Ai-Data-Operations, and there are 105 changed files. The secret scan is clean: only AWS doc example keys and 123456789012 placeholders. But "all" also covers leftovers from the Strands test run: MANUAL_DAG_*.py (bypasses the renderer and hardcodes a role ARN), run/discovery_complete.json (claims a user confirmation that never happened), the rewritten customer_orders tests and semantic.yaml, .handoffs/, logs/, and reviews/security-findings.md, which publicly lists 2 unfixed MEDIUM findings. What should go into the commit?

The Cedar agent policies deny work each ADOP agent is required to do (sub-agents writing tests, the transformation agent writing config/transformations.yaml, the quality agent writing rendered scripts, the IaC agent with no policy at all). How should I reconcile them before enforcing on Claude Code, Codex and Kiro?
Some agents have no ADOP Cedar principal: generic helpers like Explore, general-purpose and plugin agents. How should Cedar treat them?

Phase 3 profiling on Strands must be read-only against AWS. With the custom glue-athena MCP excluded, aws-mcp reaches AWS only through `run_script` (arbitrary code). How should the Strands profiler reach Glue, S3 and Athena?
